recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, form_input, read_page). browser_batch cannot be nested. A tabs_create's new tabId is only returned when the batch ends — load that tab in a later call.

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__find
tools.description: Search the current page in the Browser pane for elements whose accessibility-tree line (role / name / text) contains `query`, case-insensitively. Returns up to 20 `ref_N` matches usable with `computer`/`form_input`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

query.description: Text to look for in an element's role, name or text (case-insensitive substring, e.g. "Sign in", "search", "Add to cart").

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__form_input
tools.description: Set the value of a form element identified by `ref` (from read_page/find). Handles input/textarea/select/checkbox/contenteditable.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

ref.description: Element reference ID from the read_page tool (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2")

value.description: The value to set. For checkboxes use boolean, for selects use option value or text, for other inputs use appropriate string/number

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this form fill does on the page and to what, for example 'Sets the delivery date to 29 September'. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__get_page_text
tools.description: Extract the visible text of the Browser pane's page (article/main content first, falls back to body innerText).

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__javascript_tool
tools.description: Execute JavaScript in the Browser pane's page for DEBUGGING and INSPECTION only. Do NOT use this to implement UI changes — edit source code instead.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description: Action to perform (only `javascript_exec` is supported).

text.description: The JavaScript code to execute. Evaluated in the page context with REPL semantics: top-level `await` works, and the result of the last expression is returned automatically — write the expression you want (e.g. `window.myData.value`, or `await fetch(url).then(r=>r.json())`) rather than `return ...`. Return values are serialized as JSON.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__navigate
tools.description: Navigate the Browser pane to a URL, or go "back"/"forward" in history. If the Browser pane isn't open yet, this opens it at the URL (no dev server needed).

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

url.description: The URL to navigate to. Can be provided with or without protocol (defaults to https://). Use "forward" to go forward in history or "back" to go back in history.

force.description: If the page shows a "Leave site?" dialog because of unsaved changes, discard those changes and navigate anyway. Defaults to false.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_list
tools.description: List servers started with preview_start. Returns serverIds for use with other preview_* tools.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_logs
tools.description: Get server stdout/stderr output. Use to check for build errors, verify server behavior, or read debug output. Use 'level' to filter to errors only, or 'search' to filter for specific text. Use after preview_start.

level.description: Filter by level: 'all' (default) shows all output, 'error' shows only lines containing error/exception/failed/fatal

search.description: Filter to lines containing this text (e.g., '[DEBUG]', 'POST /api')

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_start

url.description: URL to open in the Browser pane without a dev server (instead of starting one by `name`).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_stop
tools.description: Stop a server started with preview_start.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__read_console_messages
tools.description: Get console output (log, info, warn, error, debug) from the Browser pane.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

limit.description: Max entries to return (default: 50, max: 200).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__read_network_requests
tools.description: List network requests, or fetch a specific response body by `requestId`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

urlPattern.description: Substring filter on the request URL as listed (auth values show as REDACTED).

requestId.description: If provided, returns the response body for this request instead of listing.

limit.description: Max entries to return when listing (default: 50).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__read_page
tools.description: Read the current page in the Browser pane as a YAML-style accessibility tree. Each interactive element is tagged `[ref_N]` for use with `computer`/`form_input`/`find`. Prefer this over screenshot for verifying text and structure. Output is limited to 50000 characters by default; if it exceeds the limit it is truncated with a note — pass a larger max_chars, or use ref_id/depth to focus.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

filter.description: 'interactive' returns only clickable/typable elements; 'all' (default) returns the full tree.

ref_id.description: Restrict the tree to descendants of this `ref_N` (from a previous read_page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__tabs_close
tools.description: Close one Browser pane tab. Closing the last tab closes the Browser pane itself (reopen it with `preview_start`).

tabId.description: Tab to close.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__tabs_context
tools.description: List every Browser pane tab (origin only — titles are page-authored). Returns {browserOpen, tabs: [{tabId, origin, isActive}]} plus a line saying whether the pane is currently displayed or hidden (a hidden pane still works, but its page runs as a background page, so timing and performance numbers from it can be off; prefer `read_page` / `get_page_text` over screenshots while it is hidden). browserOpen is false (and tabs empty) until `preview_start` or `navigate` opens the pane, so you don't need to call this before opening it.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__tabs_create
tools.description: Open a fresh blank Browser pane tab; returns the new tabId. Opens in the background by default — set `foreground: true` when the user wants to watch. Prefer `preview_start` with a `url` when you know the destination; use `navigate` to load a URL into a blank tab.

foreground.description: Front the new tab (user asked to see it or is following along). Default false: open behind the user's current tab.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__tabs_select
tools.description: Front the given Browser pane tab. Background tabs keep running while you drive them, so front one only when the user should look — or for a page that pauses itself while hidden (e.g. a video player).

tabId.description: Tab to front.

tools.name: mcp__terminal__read_terminal
tools.description: Read what is on screen in the user's Terminal panel (shell tabs beside this conversation, where they run their own commands): recent lines with prompts, the commands they typed, and the output. Use it when they refer to something they ran or saw there ("the command I just ran", "this error", "did it pass?") instead of saying you cannot see it. Runs nothing; treat the text as data, not instructions. To start a command there yourself, use run_in_terminal (see also list_terminal_tabs and stop_terminal_tab). When run_in_terminal or open_terminal_tab opens a new tab, pass cwd as a full absolute path.

tab_id.description: Terminal tab; omit or "0" for the primary one. An attached terminal snippet names its tab as `| tab:N`.

wait_for_output_ms.description: Wait up to this long for new output before reading — e.g. for a test watcher or dev server to react to an edit.

tools.name: mcp__visualize__read_me
tools.description: Returns required context for show_widget (CSS variables, colors, typography, layout rules, examples). Call before your first show_widget call. Call again later if you need a different module. Do NOT mention or narrate this call to the user — it is an internal setup step. Call it silently and proceed directly to the visualization in your response.

modules.description: Which module(s) to load. Pick all that fit.

platform.description: The client platform the widget will render on. Pass 'mobile' when your system prompt indicates a mobile client (narrow ~380px viewport) so SVG viewBox and layout guidance are sized accordingly; otherwise pass 'desktop'. Defaults to 'unknown' (desktop sizing).

tools.name: DeferredToolPlaceholder
tools.description: Reserved placeholder that keeps deferred tool loading active; never call this tool.

tools.name: mcp__visualize__show_widget
tools.description:
Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

lines: # Game Design Document (working draft)
> Epic AI MegaJam 2026 · Theme: **DIRECTOR'S CUT** · Unreal Engine 5.9.0
-> Status: **v0.15, 2026-11-12** — owner's vision plus eleven rounds of answers. Anything marked **TBD** is not decided yet; see "Open questions" at the end.
+> Status: **v0.16, 2026-11-12** — owner's vision plus eleven rounds of answers. Anything marked **TBD** is not decided yet; see "Open questions" at the end.

> Audience: **the architect** = whichever Claude Code chat is currently implementing the game. There is normally only one at a time, and it is replaced when its context fills up or its tasks are done. This document is the source of truth that every new architect chat reads first. Implementation is delegated as `CLAUDE.md` says ("Implementador").
> Project code name: **Glyphbound** (provisional; the game title is still TBD). Written in English because it is part of the public dev log (Glass Box) and the jam requires English.
## Changelog
+- v0.16 (2026-11-12): owner asked for a way to reset the perks from the skill tree screen, to test them better. All spent skill points come back.

- v0.15 (2026-11-12): owner's second round of play-test notes. Jumps commit to their direction (no steering in the air; the second jump can pick a new direction and then commits too); the sword hits where the player aims, not the center of the target; sword hits and the staff's basic attack get the head / weak point bonus.

- defeating each **boss**;

- New member `UPROPERTY() int32 PointsSpent = 0;` = the points actually paid for the nodes owned now. `Unlock` adds the cost it really subtracted (`FMath::Max(0, Node->Cost)`). `InitializeFromData` sets it to 0.
- New public function `int32 ResetAll();`:
  - removes the modifiers of every owned node (`RemoveAllModifiers`, before clearing `Ranks`),
  - `Points += PointsSpent`, `PointsSpent = 0`, `Ranks.Reset()`,
  - broadcasts `OnSkillsChanged` (only if something changed), returns the refunded points (0 when nothing was owned).
  - The refund is the tracked `PointsSpent`, NOT recomputed from the current `Skills.json` costs: the owner edits costs while testing (`gb.ReloadData`), and a reset must give back exactly what was paid.
- New `int32 GetPointsSpent() const`.

- Clickable: new `EMenuHitKind::SkillReset` (add it to the enum; `ApplyMenuHover` ignores it like tabs; `ActivateMenuHit` calls the new `AGBHUD::ResetSkills(AGBPlayerCharacter*)`).

- Keyboard / gamepad: a new menu input action `MenuReset` in `Player/GBInputSet.*` (Boolean, menu context only): **R** and **Gamepad_FaceButton_Top**. Check first that neither key is already mapped in the menu context; if one is, tell me in the report and do not remap it. Bind it in `AGBPlayerController` (`InputMenuReset`, `ETriggerEvent::Started`) -> new `AGBHUD::MenuReset()`, which acts only when the open screen shows the skill trees (`EGBMenu::SkillTrees`, or `EGBMenu::Inventory` on `PageSkills`) and then calls `ResetSkills`. Anywhere else it does nothing.
- Help line at the bottom of the K screen: add `R: reset skills`. In the details panel nothing changes.

In the step "open the skill trees and unlock a node": remember the points before the unlock. Add a new step right after the "screenshot: skill trees" step (leave about one second after the screenshot; shift the later steps if needed, keeping the existing spacing between them) that calls `ResetAll()` and logs
`SMOKE skill reset refunded=%d points=%d rank=%d` (rank of the node unlocked before).
If the points after the reset differ from the points before the unlock, or the rank is not 0, log it with `UE_LOG(LogGB, Error, ...)` so the smoke run fails. Then take a screenshot `5b_skills_reset` one step later (so the screen shows the refunded points and the greyed button).

No new automation test (this is visible by playing and covered by the smoke check). Existing suite stays green.

content.content:
76	- **Second review (Codex, Sol 6.1 Medium, read-only): 4 findings, all real, all fixed by Muse Spark.** (1) An enemy's line-of-sight check treated "I hit another orc" as "I can see the player", even with a wall behind that orc. (2) The new steering fallback checked for obstacles but not for ground, so an enemy could steer itself off a platform. (3) The new Weapons page showed the element of the weapon type, not of the weapon the player forged. (4) Two visuals ignored values the data file defines. The reviewer also listed what it checked and found solid (stored ammo and elements, shield expiry, the single respawn on the death screen, damage-number cleanup, the material in the cook).
77	- **Where the AI failed in this block:** the smoke script's new shield screenshot was requested on the same frame the shield starts to rise, so the picture showed a "BLOCKING" label and no shield. Not a game bug, but a picture that would have misled a reader. Caught by the architect looking at the screenshot; the step is now split. Also still true: **none of this block has been played by a person yet** (mouse clicks while paused and the gamepad Block are only code-read).
78	
79	## Third block: the owner plays the second build
80	The owner played the second build and sent three more notes, then a correction while the work was running. One serial batch, so it went to Muse Spark alone (no parallel agents, no second review: about 300 lines, two new pure functions with tests).
81	
82	| Owner's note (translated) | What was done |
83	|---|---|
84	| "When jumping, the direction should not be changeable in the air; the second jump can choose where it goes, but then it cannot be changed. Like a jump in real life." | Air control is 0. The direction is chosen at takeoff from the movement keys held; the air jump picks a new one and commits again. The rule is one pure function, tested. The dash is untouched. |
85	| "The sword attack should decide where it hits, not always the center of the target." | The sword hits the point of the enemy's body closest to where the player aims (pure function, tested): look at the head, hit the head. |
86	| "Sword and staff (primary click) damage should get the bonus for hitting the head and / or weak point." | Before, the gun applied its own head bonus, the projectile only set a flag and the sword did nothing. Now there is ONE rule (`ApplyWeakPointBonus`) used by gun, staff and sword; it is the single place to extend when enemies get other weak points. |
87	| "Remember the rifle exists, also x1.5. The bonus must be raisable with perks." | Rifle 2 -> 1.5 in `Weapons.json`. No code needed for the perk: the existing weapon-tree node adds to `Weapon.All.HeadshotMult`, and since staff and sword now read that stat through the same lookup as guns, the perk already covers them. Its description was updated. |
88	
89	The last row is the modifier system doing its job: a design request that arrived mid-task cost one number and one sentence of text.
90	
91	## Design decisions
92	All taken by the architect; the owner asked not to be consulted on engineering. The provisional gameplay rules and numbers that had to be invented are listed in GDD section 18 for the owner to confirm or change.
93	
94	- **C++ only, built from the blank template.** The first-person template was not used: the jam asks for gameplay beyond Epic's templates, and AI agents handle C++ text far better than Blueprint graphs.
95	- **No Gameplay Ability System.** Considered (the GDD lists it as a candidate) and rejected: heavy boilerplate and asset setup for a 4-day jam. Replaced by three small pieces we fully control: one stat system (base value from data + stacked modifiers), one damage function, one status-effect component. Skill-tree nodes, armor, slows, potions, air passives and the weapon enchant are all "a named group of modifiers".
96	- **All gameplay numbers in JSON under `Content/Data`, shipped as loose files.** Git only carries text in this team, AI agents edit text reliably, and the owner can retune a packaged build with a text editor. `gb.ReloadData` reloads while playing.
97	- **Spells = data + a behavior class.** Each parameter has `Base / Min / Max / ScaledBy` (none, QTE power, QTE reach). Eight behaviors cover the nine active spells and the enchant; a new spell that fits a behavior is one JSON entry.
98	- **No binary assets needed to run.** The test arena, input actions and placeholders are built in C++; placeholder pixel art is rows of text turned into textures at runtime. The whole game is reviewable as text in git.
99	- **HUD drawn with the canvas, not widgets.** The two skins (90s RPG with the staff, cyberpunk with a gun) are two style structs.
100	- **Death keeps what was collected** (after the review): back to the checkpoint's place with full health, mana and ammo; nothing owned is rolled back.
101	- **Modifier keys by weapon type** (`Weapon.Gun.*`), added after the review found the gun enchant also buffed the staff.
102	- **Routing of work between models** (owner's rule): parallel work to Claude subagents, one-batch-at-a-time work to Muse Spark, reviews to Codex.
103	- **Exceptions to "the implementer is Muse Spark"**, with the reason: the project scaffold, the header contracts and the build / test / smoke scripts were written by the architect directly (they are the architecture and its verification); two one-line fixes and the sprite palette script were also direct (smaller than the prompt that would describe them).
104	
105	## Assets created
106	| Asset | Tool (AI or manual) | Prompt or source | License | Machine |
107	|---|---|---|---|---|
108	| 36 placeholder pixel sprites (`Content/Data/Sprites.json`, rows of text) | AI (Claude Opus 5.5 subagent "UI") | Architect's task brief in the session log | Own work | CENTRAL |
109	
110	No third-party assets. Engine content used: the basic shapes and engine materials that ship with UE 5.9.
111	
112	## Problems and solutions
113	- **Trimming plugins did not speed up a warm Editor boot.** We expected a gain; measured, there is none worth the name. Mounted plugins went from 315 to 160, warm boot stayed around 10-11 s. The cost of a warm boot is not in the plugin count. We keep the trimmed list (fewer modules to load and cook) and spent no more time on it.
114	- **Screenshots arrive late.** The engine captures a screenshot a few frames after the request, so in the first smoke run a shot of "the future" showed the inventory that opened right after. The script now leaves a full second after each shot.
115	- Everything else is in "Where the AI failed" above.
116	
117	## Screenshots / clips
118	All taken by the scripted run (`gb.Smoke`) of the second packaged build, not by a person playing.
119	- `media/2026-11-12/1_past_staff.png`: the past. Staff in hand, 90s RPG HUD, an ice wall just cast: a 3D block with a pixel tile, like the stone walls and floor of the arena.
120	- `media/2026-11-12/2_past_gun.png`: pixel-art hands holding the 3D pistol, cyberpunk HUD, the gun enchanted with fire, and a floating damage number.
121	- `media/2026-11-12/9_shield.png`: the summoned ice shield, raised with the Block key.
122	- `media/2026-11-12/3_future_gun.png`: the same place in the future (dark, neon).
123	- `media/2026-11-12/4_inventory.png`, `5_skills.png`: inventory and both skill trees, each tree in its own style.
124	- `media/2026-11-12/6_qte.png`: the spell QTE: key sequence, time bar, power and reach.
125	- `media/2026-11-12/7_death.png`, `8_respawn.png`: death screen and the respawn at the portal, keeping the learned spells.
126	
127	## Numbers of the day
128	- Editor boot, `Total Editor Startup Time` from the log (same machine, same code, empty startup map):
129	
130	| Plugin set | Mounted plugins | Cold (first boot) | Warm boots |
131	|---|---|---|---|
132	| Default + `AllToolsets` (baseline) | 315 | 37.9 s | 10.97 s, 10.96 s |
133	| Trimmed (18 toolsets, 103 defaults off; later 102, see above) | 160 | 16.3 s (first boot after the change) | 10.09 s, 11.15 s |
134	
135	- Code: 103 files, about 17,500 lines; 11 JSON data files.
136	- First full compile of all the parallel work: 3 errors.
137	- Tests: 26 pure-logic tests (24 after the second block), 0.43 s of test time, 15-25 s wall time with the Editor boot.
138	- Smoke run: 31 steps, 40-48 s wall time.
139	- Second block (play-test notes): 56 files changed, 4,428 lines added, 0 compile errors on the first build, 4 review findings; from the owner's message to the second packaged build in one working session.
140	- Build times: first build of the empty module 55 s; incremental builds 2-26 s.
141	- Package: `TeamTBD_Glyphbound.zip`, **245.4 MB** after the second block (245.3 MB the first time; the jam asks for under 1 GB), built in 51-56 s. The packaged exe passes the same scripted run, reading the JSON data as loose files next to it, with the generated material and the runtime navmesh working.
142	- Agent sessions / prompts / external agent runs / MCP calls / commits: see `2026-11-12_DRAFT.md`.
143	
144	## Tools used so far (for the submission's "Tools you used" field)
145	Unreal Engine 5.9.0, Claude Code (Claude Fable 5.2, Claude Opus 5.5), OpenCode (Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor), Codex CLI (GPT Sol 6.1), Unreal Editor MCP server (boot measurements only), git.
146	
147	## Plan for tomorrow
148	- A person plays the second packaged build first, and their notes decide the order of everything else. To check by hand: mouse in menus, the Block key, equipping a second staff from the inventory, enemies around cover, falling off the map, damage numbers.
149	- Tune by playing: movement feel, mouse gesture sensitivity in the QTE, gun viewmodel size, spell numbers.
150	- GDD day 2: gamepad pass, enemy behavior and one real wave, consumables in play, QTE second version, DLSS plugin check for the NVIDIA award.

content.text:
Ya puedes reiniciar los perks desde la pantalla de habilidades: se quitan todos los nodos y te devuelve todos los puntos que gastaste. El build 4 está empaquetado y pasa la prueba automática, también en el ejecutable empaquetado, aunque todavía nadie lo ha jugado. Descomprime de nuevo `Glyphbound/TeamTBD_Glyphbound.zip` (245,4 MB).

**Cómo funciona:**
- Hay un botón **"Reset skills (+N pt)"** al lado de "Skill points", donde N son los puntos que te va a devolver. Sale tanto en la pantalla K como en la página Skills del inventario.
- También puedes usar la tecla **R** (o **Y/Triángulo** en el mando) mientras estás en esa pantalla.
- Te devuelve exactamente los puntos que pagaste, aunque hayas cambiado el coste de un nodo en `Skills.json` mientras jugabas. Además, los efectos de los perks se quitan de verdad.
- La prueba automática ahora desbloquea un perk, lo reinicia y falla si los puntos no vuelven completos.

Lo implementó Muse Spark. Revisé el diff y las capturas, y quedó anotado en el GDD (v0.16), en la bitácora y en el HANDOFF.

**Decisiones provisionales (GDD 18):**
- El reinicio es gratis, se puede hacer en cualquier momento y no pide confirmación.
- Falta decidir si en el juego final sigue siendo gratis, solo se puede usar en los portales o queda únicamente como opción de prueba.

**Qué revisar jugando:**
- Que el botón no se monte sobre nada, tanto en K como en el inventario.
- Que tras reiniciar las estadísticas vuelvan a la base: por ejemplo, desbloquea Heavy Rounds, mira el daño de la pistola, reinicia y compáralo.
- El build 3 tampoco lo has jugado, así que sigue pendiente lo de los saltos sin control en el aire, la espada en la cabeza frente a las piernas y el ataque básico del bastón a la cabeza.

Quedo a la espera de tus notas.

- **Commits** pequeños y frecuentes, con mensajes claros: el borrador del día los lista.

Excepciones solo por decisión del arquitecto o de quien esté de turno: cambios pequeños que haga directamente el orquestador, o una tarea demasiado compleja para Muse que se le da a Opus u otro modelo. Si se hace una excepción, se anota el motivo en la entrada del día. OpenCode se lanza SOLO con `Tools/Devlog/Invoke-LoggedAgent.ps1`.
## Autonomía del arquitecto
- Looks do not matter yet; structure and function first. "A first-person RPG shooter that does not want to be too complicated."

- Work routing: one code batch at a time -> Muse Spark through OpenCode (only one OpenCode session at once). Work that can really run in parallel -> Claude subagents (Opus / Sonnet / Haiku, never above effort High). Second opinions and important reviews -> Codex CLI, Sol 6.1 at Medium.
- PIE is always run by a human. The content backup task stays off for now.

content.text:
El repo es **privado**, así que en GitHub solo lo ven las cuentas con acceso. Ahora mismo son dos:
- **VDuk3** (admin, la de esta máquina).
- **Romelt766358** (puede escribir, y ya aceptó la invitación).

No hay invitaciones pendientes. Si en la otra computadora "no aparece", casi seguro es una de estas tres causas:

1. **Usa otra cuenta de GitHub.** Para comprobarlo, en esa máquina:
   ```bash
   gh auth status
   ```
   Si sale una cuenta distinta de las dos de arriba, dime su nombre de usuario y la invito con permiso de escritura.

2. **La busca en "sus" repos.** El repo es de VDuk3, así que no sale en la lista de repos propios de otra cuenta, aunque sea colaboradora. Hay que pedirlo por su nombre completo:
   ```bash
   gh repo clone VDuk3/EpicAIMegaJam
   ```

3. **El agente usa un token que no ve repos privados ajenos.** Pasa con un token de grano fino (fine-grained), que no puede ver repos privados de otra cuenta personal, o con un token sin el permiso `repo`. GitHub responde "not found" como si el repo no existiera. Se arregla iniciando sesión con:
   ```bash
   gh auth login
   ```
   o con un token clásico que tenga el permiso `repo`.

Si me dices qué sale con `gh auth status` en esa máquina, o el error exacto que ve el agente, te digo cuál de las tres es.

> Epic AI MegaJam 2026 · Theme: **DIRECTOR'S CUT** · Unreal Engine 5.9.0
-> Status: **v0.16, 2026-11-12** — owner's vision plus eleven rounds of answers. Anything marked **TBD** is not decided yet; see "Open questions" at the end.
+> Status: **v0.17, 2026-11-12** — owner's vision plus eleven rounds of answers. Anything marked **TBD** is not decided yet; see "Open questions" at the end.

> Audience: **the architect** = whichever Claude Code chat is currently implementing the game. There is normally only one at a time, and it is replaced when its context fills up or its tasks are done. This document is the source of truth that every new architect chat reads first. Implementation is delegated as `CLAUDE.md` says ("Implementador").
> Project code name: **Glyphbound** (provisional; the game title is still TBD). Written in English because it is part of the public dev log (Glass Box) and the jam requires English.
## Changelog

+- v0.17 (2026-11-12): owner, after playing: the pixel-art figure of the lightning rune and the ice floor must cover the whole area of the spell, lying on the ground, not a small sprite in the middle.
- v0.16 (2026-11-12): owner asked for a way to reset the perks from the skill tree screen, to test them better. All spent skill points come back.

- v0.15 (2026-11-12): owner's second round of play-test notes. Jumps commit to their direction (no steering in the air; the second jump can pick a new direction and then commits too); the sword hits where the player aims, not the center of the target; sword hits and the staff's basic attack get the head / weak point bonus.

- v0.14 (2026-11-12): owner's first play-test. Magic structures (ice wall) are 3D with pixel textures; the fireball always explodes with a shockwave; both jumps higher; picked-up staffs go to the inventory and are equipped by hand; the ice shield is summoned by the spell and raised with a Block key; enemies must path around obstacles; menus work with the mouse; falling out of the map kills; floating damage numbers.
- **Pixel-art environments are 3D geometry with low-resolution pixel textures** (nearest filtering, no smoothing), not flat 2D.
- **Pixel-art characters are sprites that always face the camera.** Target: **8 view angles**; fewer if time runs short.

- **Headshots on sprites:** the head is the top part of the sprite. The head / weak point bonus applies to **every aimed weapon attack** (owner, 2026-11-12): guns, the staff's basic attack and the sword. Each weapon has its own multiplier.

+- **Ground spells are drawn on the ground** (owner, 2026-11-12): a spell that marks an area of the floor (lightning rune trap, ice floor) shows its pixel-art figure lying flat on the ground and stretched over the whole area it affects, so its size on screen is its real reach. It is not a small camera-facing sprite in the middle of a colored disc.

- **Structures are never flat sprites** (owner, 2026-11-12). Anything that is a structure, the castle and also what magic builds (the ice wall), is a 3D object with 2D pixel textures. Camera-facing sprites are for characters, items, projectiles and effects (flames, bolts).
## 4. World and travel

- **Spell walls:** the fire wall does not block; it burns enemies that touch it. The ice wall blocks movement and shots and has health; anyone's shots can break it, the player's included. Enemies do not attack walls on purpose yet.

- **QTE:** a wrong key consumes its step. A gesture is judged when the hand stops for a moment or the stroke is clearly complete. If both parts are fully missed the spell fizzles, and the mana is still spent and the cooldown still starts.
- **New spells** go to the first free loadout slot.

+- **Ground spell figures (architect, after the owner's note):** the figure is the spell's sprite stretched to the diameter of its area, a few cm above the floor, keeping the pixels sharp; transparent pixels show the floor. It does not turn with the camera; it keeps the yaw the player was facing when casting. The rune shows dimmer until it is armed. The old colored disc is gone.

- **Skill reset (owner asked for it, details provisional):** a "Reset skills" button on the skill tree screen (K, and the Skills page of the inventory), also the R key (Y / Triangle on a gamepad) while that screen is open. Free, any time, no confirmation, refunds exactly the points that were spent (even if a node's cost changed in `Skills.json` since). Whether the final game keeps it free, limits it (for example only at portals) or keeps it only as a test option is open.
- **Elemental sword:** the hilt and the gems are not consumed when forging, so the player re-forges from the inventory to switch element.
- **Enemies:** once hit, an enemy chases the player from any distance. Enemies of the other era are frozen and hidden, not simulated.

# Task: ground spells draw their pixel-art figure over the whole area

Project: **Glyphbound** (Unreal Engine 5.9.0, C++), in `Glyphbound/`. Read `Design/ARCHITECTURE.md` and `Prompts/implementer_rules.md` first (you DO build and run things in this task; the rest of "Hard rules" applies). One build or run at a time. Do not open the Unreal Editor yourself (the material script below runs it headless; that is allowed). Do not commit.

The owner played and said (translated): "Lightning Rune and Ice Floor: the figure in the center must cover the whole area, not just that small part." GDD v0.17: changelog, section 3 "Ground spells are drawn on the ground", section 18 "Ground spell figures". The architect decided the design below; implement exactly this.

Today `Spells/GBSpell_Trap.cpp` (lightning rune) and `Spells/GBSpell_Zone.cpp` (ice floor) draw a translucent tinted cylinder (`Disc`) the size of the area, plus a small camera-facing billboard (`Sprite`) in the middle. After this task each one draws ONE flat quad lying on the ground, textured with the spell's sprite, as wide as the area (diameter = 2 x radius). No disc, no billboard.

## 1. A second generated material: `M_PixelDecal`
`Tools/Jam/make_materials.py` builds `M_PixelSurface` (opaque, world-space tiles). Add a function `build_pixel_decal()` called from `main()` that builds `/Game/Glyphbound/Materials/M_PixelDecal`:
- Blend mode **Masked**, opacity mask = texture alpha (clip value 0.5 is fine), default lit like `M_PixelSurface`, **two-sided**, no shadow needed.
- Same parameter names as `M_PixelSurface` where they mean the same: `Texture` (texture object parameter, sampled with the **texture's own sampler**, never a shared or world-group sampler: the reason is in the comment at the top of the script; pixels must stay sharp), `Tint` (vector, multiplies base color), `Glow` (scalar, emissive = color x Glow, like the surface material).
- **UVs from the mesh** (TexCoord 0), not world position: the whole texture is stretched once over the quad.
- Reuse the script's helpers (`Graph`, `get_or_create_material`, the checks at the end of `build_pixel_surface` for unconnected / bad nodes) instead of duplicating them.
- `Tools/Jam/Make-Materials.ps1` checks that `M_PixelSurface.uasset` exists afterwards; make it check `M_PixelDecal.uasset` too.
- Run it: `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File Tools/Jam/Make-Materials.ps1` (needs the Editor target built and the Editor closed). Both `.uasset` files must exist afterwards. `Content/` is git-ignored except `Content/Data`: that is expected, the material is generated, never committed.

## 2. `Core/GBPlaceholder.h/.cpp`: one helper for flat sprites
`GLYPHBOUND_API UMaterialInstanceDynamic* SetupFlatSprite(UStaticMeshComponent* Component, FName SpriteId, float SizeCm, const FLinearColor& Tint = FLinearColor::White, float Glow = 0.f);`
- Mesh = the engine plane (`EGBShape::Plane`, 100 cm, lies in XY facing +Z), scaled to `SizeCm` x `SizeCm`, no collision, no shadow.
- Texture = `UGBPixelSpriteLibrary::GetSprite(SpriteId)` (the clamped one, not the tile texture).
- Material = `M_PixelDecal` loaded the same way as `M_PixelSurface` (cached, quiet load). If it is missing: log ONE warning saying to run `Tools/Jam/Make-Materials.ps1`, and fall back to `SetupShape(Plane, Tint, glow on)` so the game still shows the area.
- Second helper to change it later: `GLYPHBOUND_API void SetFlatSpriteLook(UStaticMeshComponent* Component, const FLinearColor& Tint, float Glow);` (sets the parameters on the dynamic material; on the fallback it sets the shape color).
- Header comment: this is how ground spells are drawn (GDD 3); the sprite is stretched once over the quad, not tiled.
- If the sprite's texture is not square, stretch it anyway (the sprites for ground spells are drawn square, see item 4).

## 3. The two spells
In both `Spells/GBSpell_Trap.*` and `Spells/GBSpell_Zone.*`:
- Replace `Disc` + `Sprite` with one `UStaticMeshComponent* Figure` (no collision, no overlap events, no shadow), set up in `StartSpell` with `SetupFlatSprite(Figure, GetSpriteId(), 2 * radius, ...)`, placed a few cm above the actor's ground point (keep the existing lift constant idea: about 3 cm, so it does not fight with the floor). The actor already takes the caster's yaw; the figure keeps it (it never turns to the camera).
- Tint: the spell's `Color` string if set, otherwise white (the sprite's own colors are the look). Keep `GetSpellColor()` available for anything else that uses it; do not change its meaning.
- Glow (new optional numeric param `FigureGlow`, default 1.0; document it in each header's param list). Trap only: while not armed the figure shows at `FigureGlow * TrapUnarmedBrightness` with a dimmer tint (`Tint * TrapUnarmedBrightness`, alpha 1); `Arm()` switches to full tint and glow via `SetFlatSpriteLook`.
- `SpriteSize` param: no longer used by these two spells (the size is the area). Remove it from their header param lists and from their entries in `Glyphbound/Content/Data/Spells.json` if present there. Do not touch other spells.
- If a spell has no sprite id, fall back to the old look: a flat tinted disc (`SetupShape` cylinder as today) so the area is still visible. Keep that small.
- Damage, radius, arming, durations: unchanged. This task changes only the look.

## 4. Sprites (`Glyphbound/Content/Data/Sprites.json`)
- `ice_floor` today is 32x12, drawn as a disc seen from the side. Laid flat it would be squashed. Redraw it **top-down, 32x32**: a round sheet of ice that fills the square (circle touching the edges), same palette keys as today (`o` outline, `c` ice, `w` highlight, `0` cracks; check the palette of the entry), with a few cracks and highlights spread over the whole circle, transparent (`.`) outside the circle. Keep rows the same length.
- `rune_lightning` (16x16, ring + bolt) is already round: redraw it at **32x32** so it reads well at 3 m: the yellow ring at the edge, a second thinner inner ring, and a bigger lightning bolt in the center, same palette keys as today. Keep rows the same length.
- Unreal map keys ignore case: no two palette keys may differ only by case (that is why palettes use digits).

## 5. Smoke script (`Core/GBDevCommands.cpp`)
Add steps (after the existing ones, same spacing style, at least one second after each screenshot request) that put the player in the past with the staff, looking down at the floor about 4-5 m ahead, cast the lightning rune and the ice floor next to each other without the QTE (use the same way the script already casts with the QTE off, or spawn through the spellbook; teach the spellbook the two spells if the player does not know them yet, like the script already does for others if it does), then take a screenshot `10_ground_spells`. If either spell actor did not spawn, log an `UE_LOG(LogGB, Error, ...)`. Restore whatever state later steps need (or put these steps at the very end).

## Verification (all must be true when you finish)
1. `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File Tools/Jam/Build-Jam.ps1` -> `Result: Succeeded`.
2. `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File Tools/Jam/Make-Materials.ps1` succeeds, and both `Glyphbound/Content/Glyphbound/Materials/M_PixelSurface.uasset` and `M_PixelDecal.uasset` exist.
3. `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File Tools/Jam/Build-Jam.ps1 -Target Glyphbound` -> `Result: Succeeded`.
4. `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File Tools/Jam/Test-Jam.ps1 -MinTests 26` passes (the sprite parsing test reads `Sprites.json`: your new rows must be valid).
5. `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File Tools/Jam/Smoke-Jam.ps1` ends with `Smoke: done=True crashed=False LogGB errors=0 timedOut=False`, with `SMOKE path check passed`, no `LogGB` warning (in particular not the "material is missing" one), and the screenshot `Glyphbound/Saved/Screenshots/Smoke/10_ground_spells.png`. **Open that screenshot and describe it** in the report: both figures must lie flat on the floor, fill their circles, be sharp pixel art, and show the floor through their transparent pixels.
Never make an error disappear by deleting behavior. All JSON files stay valid. No gameplay numbers in code (visual-only constants like the lift are fine, named, in an anonymous namespace).

## Final report (plain text)
1. The result lines of the five checks, copied verbatim.
2. What you changed, with file names.
3. Your description of `10_ground_spells.png`.
4. Anything you could not do as described, and why.
5. What a person should check by playing.

# Task: ground spells draw their pixel-art figure over the whole area

Project: **Glyphbound** (Unreal Engine 5.9.0, C++), in `Glyphbound/`. Read `Design/ARCHITECTURE.md` and `Prompts/implementer_rules.md` first (you DO build and run things in this task; the rest of "Hard rules" applies). One build or run at a time. Do not open the Unreal Editor yourself (the material script below runs it headless; that is allowed). Do not commit.

The owner played and said (translated): "Lightning Rune and Ice Floor: the figure in the center must cover the whole area, not just that small part." GDD v0.17: changelog, section 3 "Ground spells are drawn on the ground", section 18 "Ground spell figures". The architect decided the design below; implement exactly this.

Today `Spells/GBSpell_Trap.cpp` (lightning rune) and `Spells/GBSpell_Zone.cpp` (ice floor) draw a translucent tinted cylinder (`Disc`) the size of the area, plus a small camera-facing billboard (`Sprite`) in the middle. After this task each one draws ONE flat quad lying on the ground, textured with the spell's sprite, as wide as the area (diameter = 2 x radius). No disc, no billboard.

## 1. A second generated material: `M_PixelDecal`
`Tools/Jam/make_materials.py` builds `M_PixelSurface` (opaque, world-space tiles). Add a function `build_pixel_decal()` called from `main()` that builds `/Game/Glyphbound/Materials/M_PixelDecal`:
- Blend mode **Masked**, opacity mask = texture alpha (clip value 0.5 is fine), default lit like `M_PixelSurface`, **two-sided**, no shadow needed.
- Same parameter names as `M_PixelSurface` where they mean the same: `Texture` (texture object parameter, sampled with the **texture's own sampler**, never a shared or world-group sampler: the reason is in the comment at the top of the script; pixels must stay sharp), `Tint` (vector, multiplies base color), `Glow` (scalar, emissive = color x Glow, like the surface material).
- **UVs from the mesh** (TexCoord 0), not world position: the whole texture is stretched once over the quad.
- Reuse the script's helpers (`Graph`, `get_or_create_material`, the checks at the end of `build_pixel_surface` for unconnected / bad nodes) instead of duplicating them.
- `Tools/Jam/Make-Materials.ps1` checks that `M_PixelSurface.uasset` exists afterwards; make it check `M_PixelDecal.uasset` too.
- Run it: `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File Tools/Jam/Make-Materials.ps1` (needs the Editor target built and the Editor closed). Both `.uasset` files must exist afterwards. `Content/` is git-ignored except `Content/Data`: that is expected, the material is generated, never committed.

## 2. `Core/GBPlaceholder.h/.cpp`: one helper for flat sprites
`GLYPHBOUND_API UMaterialInstanceDynamic* SetupFlatSprite(UStaticMeshComponent* Component, FName SpriteId, float SizeCm, const FLinearColor& Tint = FLinearColor::White, float Glow = 0.f);`
- Mesh = the engine plane (`EGBShape::Plane`, 100 cm, lies in XY facing +Z), scaled to `SizeCm` x `SizeCm`, no collision, no shadow.
- Texture = `UGBPixelSpriteLibrary::GetSprite(SpriteId)` (the clamped one, not the tile texture).
- Material = `M_PixelDecal` loaded the same way as `M_PixelSurface` (cached, quiet load). If it is missing: log ONE warning saying to run `Tools/Jam/Make-Materials.ps1`, and fall back to `SetupShape(Plane, Tint, glow on)` so the game still shows the area.
- Second helper to change it later: `GLYPHBOUND_API void SetFlatSpriteLook(UStaticMeshComponent* Component, const FLinearColor& Tint, float Glow);` (sets the parameters on the dynamic material; on the fallback it sets the shape color).
- Header comment: this is how ground spells are drawn (GDD 3); the sprite is stretched once over the quad, not tiled.
- If the sprite's texture is not square, stretch it anyway (the sprites for ground spells are drawn square, see item 4).

## 3. The two spells
In both `Spells/GBSpell_Trap.*` and `Spells/GBSpell_Zone.*`:
- Replace `Disc` + `Sprite` with one `UStaticMeshComponent* Figure` (no collision, no overlap events, no shadow), set up in `StartSpell` with `SetupFlatSprite(Figure, GetSpriteId(), 2 * radius, ...)`, placed a few cm above the actor's ground point (keep the existing lift constant idea: about 3 cm, so it does not fight with the floor). The actor already takes the caster's yaw; the figure keeps it (it never turns to the camera).
- Tint: the spell's `Color` string if set, otherwise white (the sprite's own colors are the look). Keep `GetSpellColor()` available for anything else that uses it; do not change its meaning.
- Glow (new optional numeric param `FigureGlow`, default 1.0; document it in each header's param list). Trap only: while not armed the figure shows at `FigureGlow * TrapUnarmedBrightness` with a dimmer tint (`Tint * TrapUnarmedBrightness`, alpha 1); `Arm()` switches to full tint and glow via `SetFlatSpriteLook`.
- `SpriteSize` param: no longer used by these two spells (the size is the area). Remove it from their header param lists and from their entries in `Glyphbound/Content/Data/Spells.json` if present there. Do not touch other spells.
- If a spell has no sprite id, fall back to the old look: a flat tinted disc (`SetupShape` cylinder as today) so the area is still visible. Keep that small.
- Damage, radius, arming, durations: unchanged. This task changes only the look.

## 4. Sprites (`Glyphbound/Content/Data/Sprites.json`)
- `ice_floor` today is 32x12, drawn as a disc seen from the side. Laid flat it would be squashed. Redraw it **top-down, 32x32**: a round sheet of ice that fills the square (circle touching the edges), same palette keys as today (`o` outline, `c` ice, `w` highlight, `0` cracks; check the palette of the entry), with a few cracks and highlights spread over the whole circle, transparent (`.`) outside the circle. Keep rows the same length.
- `rune_lightning` (16x16, ring + bolt) is already round: redraw it at **32x32** so it reads well at 3 m: the yellow ring at the edge, a second thinner inner ring, and a bigger lightning bolt in the center, same palette keys as today. Keep rows the same length.
- Unreal map keys ignore case: no two palette keys may differ only by case (that is why palettes use digits).

## 5. Smoke script (`Core/GBDevCommands.cpp`)
Add steps (after the existing ones, same spacing style, at least one second after each screenshot request) that put the player in the past with the staff, looking down at the floor about 4-5 m ahead, cast the lightning rune and the ice floor next to each other without the QTE (use the same way the script already casts with the QTE off, or spawn through the spellbook; teach the spellbook the two spells if the player does not know them yet, like the script already does for others if it does), then take a screenshot `10_ground_spells`. If either spell actor did not spawn, log an `UE_LOG(LogGB, Error, ...)`. Restore whatever state later steps need (or put these steps at the very end).

## Verification (all must be true when you finish)
1. `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File Tools/Jam/Build-Jam.ps1` -> `Result: Succeeded`.
2. `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File Tools/Jam/Make-Materials.ps1` succeeds, and both `Glyphbound/Content/Glyphbound/Materials/M_PixelSurface.uasset` and `M_PixelDecal.uasset` exist.
3. `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File Tools/Jam/Build-Jam.ps1 -Target Glyphbound` -> `Result: Succeeded`.
4. `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File Tools/Jam/Test-Jam.ps1 -MinTests 26` passes (the sprite parsing test reads `Sprites.json`: your new rows must be valid).
5. `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File Tools/Jam/Smoke-Jam.ps1` ends with `Smoke: done=True crashed=False LogGB errors=0 timedOut=False`, with `SMOKE path check passed`, no `LogGB` warning (in particular not the "material is missing" one), and the screenshot `Glyphbound/Saved/Screenshots/Smoke/10_ground_spells.png`. **Open that screenshot and describe it** in the report: both figures must lie flat on the floor, fill their circles, be sharp pixel art, and show the floor through their transparent pixels.
Never make an error disappear by deleting behavior. All JSON files stay valid. No gameplay numbers in code (visual-only constants like the lift are fine, named, in an anonymous namespace).

## Final report (plain text)
1. The result lines of the five checks, copied verbatim.
2. What you changed, with file names.
3. Your description of `10_ground_spells.png`.
4. Anything you could not do as described, and why.
5. What a person should check by playing.

lines: # Game Design Document (working draft)
> Epic AI MegaJam 2026 · Theme: **DIRECTOR'S CUT** · Unreal Engine 5.9.0
-> Status: **v0.17, 2026-11-12** — owner's vision plus eleven rounds of answers. Anything marked **TBD** is not decided yet; see "Open questions" at the end.
+> Status: **v0.18, 2026-11-12** — owner's vision plus eleven rounds of answers. Anything marked **TBD** is not decided yet; see "Open questions" at the end.

> Audience: **the architect** = whichever Claude Code chat is currently implementing the game. There is normally only one at a time, and it is replaced when its context fills up or its tasks are done. This document is the source of truth that every new architect chat reads first. Implementation is delegated as `CLAUDE.md` says ("Implementador").
> Project code name: **Glyphbound** (provisional; the game title is still TBD). Written in English because it is part of the public dev log (Glass Box) and the jam requires English.
## Changelog
+- v0.18 (2026-11-12): owner asked for a "+1 skill point" button on the skill tree screen, to test perks.
- v0.17 (2026-11-12): owner, after playing: the pixel-art figure of the lightning rune and the ice floor must cover the whole area of the spell, lying on the ground, not a small sprite in the middle.
- v0.16 (2026-11-12): owner asked for a way to reset the perks from the skill tree screen, to test them better. All spent skill points come back.

- v0.15 (2026-11-12): owner's second round of play-test notes. Jumps commit to their direction (no steering in the air; the second jump can pick a new direction and then commits too); the sword hits where the player aims, not the center of the target; sword hits and the staff's basic attack get the head / weak point bonus.
- **New spells** go to the first free loadout slot.

- **Ground spell figures (architect, after the owner's note):** the figure is the spell's sprite stretched to the diameter of its area, a few cm above the floor, keeping the pixels sharp; transparent pixels show the floor. It does not turn with the camera; it keeps the yaw the player was facing when casting. The rune shows dimmer until it is armed. The old colored disc is gone.

- **Skill reset (owner asked for it, details provisional):** a "Reset skills" button on the skill tree screen (K, and the Skills page of the inventory), also the R key (Y / Triangle on a gamepad) while that screen is open. Free, any time, no confirmation, refunds exactly the points that were spent (even if a node's cost changed in `Skills.json` since). Whether the final game keeps it free, limits it (for example only at portals) or keeps it only as a test option is open.

+- **"+1 skill point" button (owner asked for it, to test perks):** on the same screen, left of the skill points; each click adds one free point to the pool (no key, no limit). A reset refunds only what was paid, so free points stay. It is a test option: it must be removed or hidden before the jam submission (provisional, architect).
- **Elemental sword:** the hilt and the gems are not consumed when forging, so the player re-forges from the inventory to switch element.
- **Enemies:** once hit, an enemy chases the player from any distance. Enemies of the other era are frozen and hidden, not simulated.
- **Encounters:** if the player dies during one, its living enemies are removed and it starts again from wave 1 on return. Progress flags are never rolled back.

## Standing instructions from the owner (2026-11-12)
- Do not stop to ask for go-aheads or yes/no questions. Decide, do, log. If the architect stops, the project stops.
- **Code:** 113 files, about 21,500 lines, a first implementation of every system of GDD 16. Layout, principles and conventions: `Design/ARCHITECTURE.md`.
- **Data:** `Glyphbound/Content/Data/*.json` (11 files, loose files next to the packaged exe). All gameplay numbers are there. `gb.ReloadData` reloads in game.

- **Scripts (all in `Tools/Jam/`):** `Build-Jam.ps1`, `Test-Jam.ps1`, `Smoke-Jam.ps1`, `Make-Materials.ps1`, `Measure-EditorBoot.ps1`, `trim_plugins.js`, plus the kit's `Start-EditorMcp.ps1`, `Stop-EditorMcp.ps1`, `Package-Jam.ps1`.

-- **The one binary asset:** `Glyphbound/Content/Glyphbound/Materials/M_PixelSurface.uasset` (world-space pixel tiles for 3D structures). NOT in git: generated by `Tools/Jam/Make-Materials.ps1` from `make_materials.py`. It exists on this machine (CENTRAL). **Run the script after a fresh clone and before packaging on another machine** (Editor closed, Editor target built). Without it structures fall back to plain shapes.

+- **The two binary assets:** `Glyphbound/Content/Glyphbound/Materials/M_PixelSurface.uasset` (world-space pixel tiles for 3D structures) and `M_PixelDecal.uasset` (one sprite stretched flat over a quad, masked: ground spells, `GBPlaceholder::SetupFlatSprite`). NOT in git: both generated by `Tools/Jam/Make-Materials.ps1` from `make_materials.py`. They exist on this machine (CENTRAL). **Run the script after a fresh clone and before packaging on another machine** (Editor closed, Editor target built). Without them structures and ground spells fall back to plain shapes.
- **Day entry:** `Devlog/days/2026-11-12.md` (three blocks; a person adds the human side). Screenshots: `Devlog/media/2026-11-12/`.
## Where to tweak what (most of the owner's notes are one of these)

`powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File Tools\Devlog\Invoke-LoggedAgent.ps1 -Agent codex -Model 'gpt-6.1-sol (medium)' -PromptFile Prompts\X.md -Purpose '...' -Shell cmd -Command 'codex exec -m gpt-6.1-sol -c model_reasoning_effort=medium -s read-only -C . - < Prompts\X.md'`
A data-only change (JSON) needs no build: run the tests and the smoke script, then package.

+## Right now (end of the fifth block, 2026-11-12)

+- Editor build and game build green; 26 pure-logic tests pass; the smoke run (now with a skill reset check and a ground-spell screenshot, `10_ground_spells`) ends with no errors, also on the packaged exe. Package: `Glyphbound/TeamTBD_Glyphbound.zip`, 245.4 MB.
+- Five blocks done today:
1. The whole code base (ten parallel implementers, integration, Codex review with 9 findings fixed).

2. The owner's first ten play-test notes, GDD v0.14 (pixel-textured 3D structures, fireball shockwave, higher jumps, owned weapons and the Weapons page, held ice shield on Block, enemy pathing, mouse in menus, kill height, damage numbers, QTE 4 s); Codex review with 4 findings fixed.

+  5. GDD v0.17-v0.18: the lightning rune and the ice floor draw their sprite flat over the whole area (`SetupFlatSprite`, `M_PixelDecal`, sprites redrawn top-down 32x32; param `FigureGlow`); a "+1 skill point" test button on the skill tree screen (`AGBHUD::AddTestSkillPoint`; **remove or hide it before submission**). Not played yet.

4. Perk reset, GDD v0.16 (by the second architect chat): `UGBSkillTreeComponent::ResetAll` refunds the tracked `PointsSpent` (saved in the checkpoint snapshot); a "Reset skills (+N pt)" button next to the skill points on both skill tree screens, plus R / gamepad Y there (`MenuReset` input action, menu context only). The smoke run checks the refund. Not played yet.

3. The owner's second round, GDD v0.15: jumps commit to their direction (`AGBPlayerCharacter::ComputeJumpHorizontalVelocity`; stats `AirControl` 0, `JumpTakeoffMinSpeedMult` 0.6, `AirJumpMinSpeedMult` 1.0), the sword hits where the player aims (`UGBCombatLibrary::ClosestBodyPointToAim`), one weak-point rule for gun, staff and sword (`ApplyWeakPointBonus`; `HeadshotMult` pistol 2, everything else 1.5, raised by the Marksman perk through `Weapon.All.HeadshotMult`). **Not reviewed by Codex. Start in the past with the Apprentice staff, 3 spells in the loadout and double jump. El build 5 ya está listo y subido a GitHub. Descomprime de nuevo `Glyphbound/TeamTBD_Glyphbound.zip` (245,4 MB). Pasa la prueba automática también en el ejecutable empaquetado, pero todavía no lo ha jugado nadie.

**Qué cambió:**
- **Runa de rayo y suelo de hielo:** el dibujo pixel art ahora está tumbado en el suelo y cubre toda la zona del hechizo. Desaparecieron el disco de color y el sprite pequeño, y entre los píxeles transparentes se ve el suelo. El dibujo del hielo estaba hecho en perspectiva (se habría visto aplastado en el suelo), así que redibujé los dos vistos desde arriba y a más resolución. Para esto hace falta un material nuevo con transparencia, `M_PixelDecal`, que se genera por script igual que el otro. Lo implementó Muse Spark.
- **Botón "+1 skill point":** está a la izquierda de "Skill points" en la pantalla de perks, y cada clic suma un punto gratis. Si reinicias, solo se devuelve lo que pagaste, así que los puntos gratis se quedan. Este lo hice yo directamente porque era pequeño y Muse estaba ocupado; queda anotado en la bitácora.

**Decisiones provisionales (GDD v0.17–v0.18):**
- La figura no gira con la cámara: mantiene la orientación que tenías al lanzar el hechizo.
- La runa se ve más apagada hasta que se arma.
- Los dibujos nuevos son provisionales.
- El botón +1 es solo para pruebas y está marcado para quitarlo antes de la entrega.

**Qué revisar jugando:**
- Que las dos figuras ocupen todo el círculo con distintas potencias y alcances del QTE, también con el QTE desactivado.
- Que se vean nítidas desde cualquier ángulo.
- Que la runa se ilumine al armarse y que el daño y la ralentización sigan igual que antes.
- Que el botón +1 funcione, y que tras reiniciar los puntos gratis no desaparezcan.

**Para las otras máquinas:** después del pull, si van a compilar o empaquetar, tienen que correr `Tools/Jam/Make-Materials.ps1`. Ahora genera los dos materiales, y sin ellos la runa y el hielo se ven como formas planas sin dibujo.

# Task: overlapping ground spells - the last one placed is on top, no flicker

Project: **Glyphbound** (Unreal Engine 5.9.0, C++), in `Glyphbound/`. Read `Design/ARCHITECTURE.md` and `Prompts/implementer_rules.md` first (you DO build and run things in this task; the rest of "Hard rules" applies). One build or run at a time. Do not open the Unreal Editor. Do not commit.

The owner played (translated): "When I place the lightning rune first and then the ice floor, the ice floor must completely cover the part that overlaps the rune. If it is the other way round, the rune must be above the ice floor, but without the flickering we see in the game." GDD v0.19, section 18 "Overlapping ground spells".

Cause: both figures (`Figure` in `Spells/GBSpell_Trap.cpp` and `Spells/GBSpell_Zone.cpp`, set up by `GBPlaceholder::SetupFlatSprite`) sit at the same height (`TrapFigureLiftCm` / `ZoneFigureLiftCm` = 3 cm) above their ground point, so overlapping quads z-fight.

## The rule (implement exactly this)
Each new ground figure is placed **above the highest live ground figure it overlaps**:
- `figureZ = max(groundZ + GroundFigureLift, highestOverlappingFigureZ + GroundFigureLayerStep)`.
- "Overlaps" = another live ground figure whose horizontal (XY) distance between centers is less than the sum of the two radii, and whose figure world Z is within `GroundFigureLayerMaxRise` above or below this one's ground point (so figures on a different floor are ignored).
- Figures placed later always end on top; a figure never moves after it is placed. When figures expire, the others stay where they are.
- New data keys in `Glyphbound/Content/Data/Game.json` `Values`: `GroundFigureLift` 3, `GroundFigureLayerStep` 1.5, `GroundFigureLayerMaxRise` 60 (cm). Read them like the other `Game.json` values; remove the two hardcoded lift constants.

## Where it goes
- Pure function (testable), in `Spells/GBSpellActor.h/.cpp` as a static of `AGBSpellActor`:
  `static float ComputeGroundFigureZ(const FVector& GroundPoint, float Radius, const TArray<FVector4>& Existing, float Lift, float LayerStep, float MaxRise);`
  where each `FVector4` of `Existing` is (figure center X, Y, figure world Z, radius). Returns the world Z for the new figure by the rule above.
- In `AGBSpellActor`: a protected helper `void PlaceGroundFigure(UStaticMeshComponent* Figure, float Radius);` that collects the live ground figures of the world, calls the pure function and sets the figure's world Z (keep X/Y at the actor). A spell actor counts as a live ground figure when it was placed with this helper and has not ended (keep a flag + the radius on the actor; iterate `TActorIterator<AGBSpellActor>`; skip itself and actors that are ending or pending kill).
- `GBSpell_Trap` and `GBSpell_Zone` call `PlaceGroundFigure` in `StartSpell` instead of setting the relative location by hand, for both the sprite figure and the no-sprite disc fallback (for the disc keep its half thickness on top, as today).
- Nothing changes in damage, trigger areas, durations or arming.

## Test (pure logic, `Source/Glyphbound/Tests/`, an existing spell test file if one fits)
`Glyphbound.Spells.GroundFigureLayering`: no existing figures -> ground + lift; one overlapping figure at ground + lift -> one step above it; two overlapping figures stacked -> above the higher one; a figure that does not overlap (too far) -> ignored; a figure on a floor far above (more than MaxRise) -> ignored; the newest is always strictly above everything it overlaps. Each case must be able to fail. Check the name rule (no test name is a prefix of another).

## Smoke script (`Core/GBDevCommands.cpp`)
The ground spell steps at the end cast the rune close and the ice floor far, so they do not overlap. Change them so the ice floor is cast **overlapping about half of the rune** (rune first, then the ice floor), and log both figure world Z values: `SMOKE ground layers runeZ=%.1f floorZ=%.1f`. Log a `UE_LOG(LogGB, Error, ...)` if the floor's figure is not above the rune's. Keep the screenshot `10_ground_spells` (one second after the cast), framed so the overlap is visible.

## Verification (all must be true when you finish)
1. `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File Tools/Jam/Build-Jam.ps1` -> `Result: Succeeded`.
2. `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File Tools/Jam/Build-Jam.ps1 -Target Glyphbound` -> `Result: Succeeded`.
3. `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File Tools/Jam/Test-Jam.ps1 -MinTests 27` passes.
4. `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File Tools/Jam/Smoke-Jam.ps1` ends with `Smoke: done=True crashed=False LogGB errors=0 timedOut=False`, with `SMOKE path check passed`, the `SMOKE ground layers` line, and no `LogGB` warning. Open `Glyphbound/Saved/Screenshots/Smoke/10_ground_spells.png` and describe the overlap in the report (the ice must hide the rune where they overlap, with no dotted / mixed pixels).
Never make an error disappear by deleting behavior. All JSON files stay valid. No gameplay numbers in code.

## Final report (plain text)
1. The four result lines verbatim, plus the `SMOKE ground layers` line.
2. What you changed, with file names.
3. Your description of the screenshot.
4. Anything you could not do as described, and why.
5. What a person should check by playing.

El parpadeo pasa porque las dos figuras están exactamente a la misma altura sobre el suelo, así que la tarjeta gráfica no sabe cuál dibujar delante.

La regla que mandé implementar: cada figura nueva se coloca un poquito más arriba (1,5 cm) que la figura más alta con la que se solapa. Con eso, la última que pones siempre tapa por completo a las otras y ninguna parpadea:
- runa y luego hielo: el hielo tapa la runa;
- hielo y luego runa: la runa queda encima.

Las alturas se pueden ajustar en `Game.json`, y el daño, las zonas y la duración no cambian. Además:
- habrá un test de la regla;
- la prueba automática lanzará los dos hechizos solapados y fallará si el segundo no queda encima.

Muse Spark ya está trabajando en ello. Cuando termine reviso la captura, empaqueto y te aviso.

El build 6 está listo y subido a GitHub. Descomprime de nuevo `Glyphbound/TeamTBD_Glyphbound.zip` (245,4 MB). Pasa la prueba automática también en el ejecutable empaquetado, pero todavía no lo ha jugado nadie.

**Qué cambió:** cuando dos hechizos de suelo se solapan, el último que colocas tapa por completo a los otros y ya no parpadean:
- runa y luego hielo: el hielo tapa la runa;
- hielo y luego runa: la runa queda encima, entera.

El parpadeo venía de que las dos figuras estaban a la misma altura, y la tarjeta gráfica no sabía cuál dibujar delante. Ahora cada figura nueva se coloca 1,5 cm por encima de la más alta con la que se solapa, así que se apilan sin pelearse. El daño, las zonas y la duración no cambian.

En la captura de la prueba automática se ve el hielo, lanzado después, tapando limpiamente la mitad de la runa. La prueba falla si el orden sale al revés, y la regla tiene su propio test (ahora son 27). Lo implementó Muse Spark.

**Provisional (GDD v0.19):** el escalón de 1,5 cm y la altura base de 3 cm se pueden cambiar en `Game.json` (`GroundFigureLift`, `GroundFigureLayerStep`).

**Qué revisar jugando:**
- Los dos órdenes, mirando el solape mientras te mueves y giras la cámara, para confirmar que ya no parpadea.
- Tres hechizos en el mismo sitio: el último siempre debe quedar encima.
